entities.name: Chronic nonbacterial osteomyelitis
observations: Pediatric chronic or recurrent bone inflammation can cause metaphyseal osteolytic lesions, periosteal reaction, marrow edema, pain, fever, and elevated inflammatory markers; infection and malignancy must be excluded.
In a clinically stable child with atypical or multifocal-appearing lesions, biopsy is used to establish diagnosis and exclude bacterial infection or malignancy before anti-inflammatory treatment.

source_tools.relevance: Focused pediatric search for differential diagnosis and tissue diagnosis

entities.name: Acute hematogenous osteomyelitis
observations: Typical management includes blood cultures and prompt empiric antibiotics in a clinically ill child; aspiration or biopsy is considered when the diagnosis is uncertain, lesions are atypical, or microbiologic confirmation is needed.
MRI findings of marrow edema and periosteal elevation support osteomyelitis but are not specific for infection.

entities.name: Atypical pediatric femoral lesions require tissue diagnosis
observations: A well-appearing child with subacute fever, focal bone pain, and multiple metaphyseal osteolytic lesions has an atypical presentation in which malignancy and chronic nonbacterial osteomyelitis remain important alternatives to bacterial osteomyelitis.
Bone biopsy is the most definitive next diagnostic step among the listed choices when diagnosis is uncertain and treatment should not be started empirically.

source_tools.relevance: Synthesis of focused pediatric osteomyelitis and chronic nonbacterial osteomyelitis search
